hero.h1: ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant in Bangalore
hero.intro: ARTAS uses image-guided robotics to assist our doctors during hair transplantation. The robot supports the steps that need precision and repetition. Your doctor still designs the hairline and makes every decision.

intro.h2: What Is ARTAS Robotic Hair Restoration?
paragraphs: ARTAS is a robotic system used in follicular unit extraction (FUE) hair transplants. It uses a high-definition, multi-camera vision system to identify healthy follicular units in the donor area. A robotic arm then helps the doctor harvest them and create the recipient sites.
The robot is a tool. It does not decide who is treated or how the hairline looks. That is your doctor's role.
Whether ARTAS suits you depends on your hair-loss pattern, donor density, scalp condition and hair characteristics. We assess these first.

steps.title: Assessment and planning
steps.text: Your doctor reviews your hair loss, donor area and goals, then designs the hairline.

steps.title: Image-guided mapping
steps.text: The vision system scans the donor area and identifies follicular units suited to harvest.

steps.title: Precise harvesting
steps.text: The robotic arm assists with extracting individual grafts, one at a time, with consistent movements.

steps.title: Recipient-site creation
steps.text: Sites are created to follow your planned hairline, direction and density.

steps.title: Implantation
steps.text: Grafts are placed by our team according to the plan.

steps.title: Aftercare
steps.text: You leave with written instructions and a follow-up schedule.

cards.title: Image-guided precision
cards.text: Each graft is chosen using imaging, not by eye alone.

cards.title: Consistent harvesting
cards.text: The robotic arm repeats the same movement without fatigue.

cards.title: No strip incision
cards.text: Grafts are taken one by one, so there is no linear strip scar as with FUT. Tiny marks at the donor area are expected.

cards.title: No stitches or staples
cards.text: No stitches or staples are needed for graft extraction.

cards.title: Personalised planning
cards.text: Hairline, density and placement follow your face and your long-term hair-loss pattern.

cards.title: Doctor-led at every step
cards.text: The robot assists. The doctor decides.

benefits.smallPrint: Results, recovery and visible growth vary from person to person.

candidates.lead: ARTAS may suit men and women with androgenetic (pattern) hair loss who have enough healthy donor hair. Your doctor checks:
items: Pattern and stage of hair loss
paragraphs: Some hair types and areas are better treated with manual FUE or DHI. We recommend what fits, not what is newest.

Transplanted hairs usually shed in the first few weeks. New growth then starts and builds gradually over several months. Your doctor reviews progress at set stages of the growth cycle. Final density and appearance vary between patients.

cost.h2: Cost of ARTAS Hair Transplant in Bangalore
paragraphs: The cost depends on the number of grafts, the area treated, your plan, the number of sessions and follow-up. A preliminary estimate may be shared after your records are reviewed. The final cost follows your in-person assessment.

faqs.h2: Frequently Asked Questions About ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant

items.q: What is ARTAS?
items.a: A robotic system that assists doctors in FUE hair transplants. It uses imaging to identify grafts and a robotic arm to help harvest them.

items.q: Does the robot perform the surgery?
items.a: No. Your doctor plans the hairline, supervises every step and makes every decision. The robot assists with precise, repetitive tasks.

items.q: Does ARTAS leave a linear scar?
items.a: No. Grafts are extracted one by one, with no strip removed. Small dot marks remain at the donor area and are usually covered by hair.

items.q: How is ARTAS different from manual FUE?
items.a: Both take grafts individually. In manual FUE, the operator's hand does the extraction. In ARTAS, a robotic arm helps with consistent movements.

items.q: Is ARTAS suitable for everyone?
items.a: No. Suitability depends on donor density, hair type, scalp condition and your pattern of loss. The doctor decides at consultation.

items.q: Does ARTAS work for women?
items.a: It can for suitable candidates with pattern hair loss and enough donor hair. Your doctor will advise.

items.q: Is ARTAS painful?
items.a: The area is numbed with local anaesthesia. Most patients feel pressure rather than sharp pain. Comfort varies.

items.q: How long does the procedure take?
items.a: It depends on the number of grafts. Most sessions take one day. Your doctor confirms timing in your plan.

items.q: When will I see results?
items.a: Growth is gradual. Many patients see early growth after three to four months and fuller results by 12 months or more. Results vary.

items.q: How soon can I return to work?
items.a: Many patients return within a few days. Your doctor will advise based on your plan.

items.q: Is it permanent?
items.a: Transplanted follicles from the donor area are generally long-lasting. Existing hair can still thin, so a maintenance plan may help.

closing.h2: Find Out If ARTAS Is Right for You
closing.paragraph: Book a consultation. Your doctor will assess your hair and donor area and give an honest plan.

disclaimer.text: Results vary from person to person. This page is for patient education and does not replace an in-person consultation. Medically reviewed by Dr. Sandeep Mahapatra.

items.q: Can I have a consultation before I travel?
items.a: Yes. Online consultations can begin before you travel. Some treatments need an in-person assessment first, and your doctor tells you which.

items.q: How many days do I need to stay in Bangalore?
items.a: It depends on your treatment, the number of visits and the recovery review. We discuss this with you before travel dates are finalised.

items.q: Can you help with my visa and travel?
items.a: Visa, travel and accommodation are arranged by the patient. We share the visit plan and clinic details to help you prepare.

items.q: Will someone help me during my stay?
items.a: Your care team stays in touch before, during and after treatment.

items.q: Can I send photos before I come?
items.a: Yes. Photos help your doctor give an initial opinion. A final plan is made after a full consultation.

items.q: How soon can I fly home after treatment?
items.a: Your doctor advises based on the treatment and how you are healing. Most patients get a clear date in their plan.

items.q: What does the cost include?
items.a: A preliminary estimate may be shared after records review. The final cost follows the in-person assessment and covers your treatment plan, visits and aftercare. Your written estimate lists what is included.

items.q: Can I continue follow-ups from my own country?
items.a: Yes. We review your progress by video, phone, WhatsApp or email.

items.q: Can I combine more than one treatment in one trip?
items.a: Often, yes. Your doctor decides what is safe to combine and in what order.

items.q: Is the result permanent?
items.a: That depends on the treatment. Some results are long-lasting. Others need maintenance. Your doctor explains this before you decide.

items.q: Which languages do you support?
items.a: English, Hindi and Kannada.

items.q: Is it safe to travel for treatment?
items.a: We follow strict clinical and hygiene protocols, and every treatment is led by a qualified doctor. We also plan your timing so you travel only when it is safe for you.
